evals.name: security-review-mandatory-consult
evals.prompt: In Claude Code, review this auth middleware change for privilege escalation risk. The advisor is configured. Give me findings only after you have done the review.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the relevant code first, then consults the configured advisor before final security findings.

assertions.text: Treats security review as a mandatory advisor-consult category when advisor is configured

evals.name: no-advisor-configured-negative
evals.prompt: In Claude Code, make this tiny typo fix. There is no advisorModel configured and no advisor tool in the session.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not call or simulate the advisor and completes the routine task normally.

assertions.text: Does not call an advisor when no advisor model or tool is configured
Does not ask the user to configure advisor for a trivial task

evals.name: non-claude-harness-negative
evals.prompt: Running in Codex, perform a code review and use claude-code-auto-advisor if useful.
evals.expected_output: The agent exits the skill because the harness is not Claude Code and does not simulate advisor with other tools.

assertions.text: Does not use the advisor policy outside Claude Code
Does not replace advisor with subagents, web search, or another model

evals.name: recurring-failure-edge
evals.prompt: In Claude Code with advisor configured, the same migration test has failed after two plausible fixes. What should you do before trying a third approach?
evals.expected_output: The agent gathers the failure evidence and consults the advisor before another speculative fix.

assertions.text: Treats recurring failure after two credible attempts as an advisor-consult trigger
Consults after collecting logs/tests rather than immediately with no context

evals.name: mechanics-disclosure
evals.prompt: In Claude Code, how do I know whether advisorModel in settings is enough to call the advisor for this session?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the mechanics reference and explains that visible settings are not sufficient if model pairing, provider, allowlist, disable flags, or actual tool attachment block advisor use.

assertions.text: Mentions that the callable advisor tool is stronger evidence than local settings

evals.name: high-level-plan-validation
evals.prompt: In Claude Code with advisor configured, I drafted a high-level implementation plan for a broad auth/session migration across middleware, API routes, tests, and deployment config. Before I start editing files, what does this skill require?
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the concrete high-level plan as a mandatory advisor-consult case, gathers the plan evidence and constraints, and consults before implementation begins.

assertions.text: Treats high-level planning validation for substantial work as an advisor-consult trigger
Requires several dependent steps or affected subsystems rather than generic planning
Consults after a concrete draft plan exists and before implementation starts

evals.name: ordinary-planning-negative
evals.prompt: In Claude Code with advisor configured, I need a quick plan for a one-file typo fix and then the next command to run. Should the advisor be consulted because this is planning?
evals.expected_output: The agent does not consult the advisor because ordinary planning, small todo lists, and one-step or two-step plans are outside the planning-validation trigger.

assertions.text: Does not treat ordinary planning as a high-level planning validation trigger
Skips advisor for one-step or two-step plans without substantial blast radius
